title: Leonurine alleviates acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury by regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in mice.
authors: Yu, Yajie; Zhou, Shizhe; Wang, Yan; Di, Shuting; Wang, Yingluo; Huang, Xin; Chen, Ying
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药单体Leonurine通过PI3K/AKT通路缓解对乙酰氨基酚肝损伤，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Leonurine (Leo) is a natural alkaloid isolated from the herb Leonurus japonicus Houtt. (Leonuri) that has been shown to inhibit oxidative stress and inflammation. However, the role and mechanism of Leo in acetaminophen (APAP)-induced acute liver injury (ALI) remain unknown. In this study, we investigated the protective effect of Leo against APAP-induced ALI and elucidated the molecular mechanism. Here, we showed that the damage to mouse primary hepatocytes (MPHs) induced by APAP was attenuated by treatment with Leo, which promoted proliferation and inhibited oxidative stress injury, and Leo significantly improved APAP-induced ALI in mice. Leo could protect against APAP-induced ALI by reducing serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine transaminase (ALT) levels, hepatic histopathological damage, liver cell necrosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress-induced damage in vivo and in vitro. Moreover, the results indicated that Leo relieved APAP-induced liver cell necrosis by reducing the expression of Bax and cleaved caspase-3 and increasing Bcl-2 expression. Leo alleviated APAP-induced oxidative stress-induced damage by activating the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) pathway, which facilitated Nrf2 nuclear translocation and upregulated oxidative stress-related protein expression in liver tissues. Moreover, the results suggested that APAP-induced inflammation in the liver was suppressed by Leo by suppressing the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and NLR family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) pathways. In addition, Leo facilitated the activation of the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/AKT signaling pathway in the liver tissue of ALI mice. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and western blotting showed that PI3K was a potential target of Leo in the treatment of ALI. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) indicated that Leo could stably bind to the PI3K protein. In conclusion, Leo attenuated ALI, and reversed liver cell necrosis, the inflammatory response and oxidative stress-induced damage by regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 益母草碱（Leo）是从植物益母草（Leonurus japonicus Houtt.）中分离出的一种天然生物碱，已被证明能抑制氧化应激和炎症。然而，Leo在对乙酰氨基酚（APAP）诱导的急性肝损伤（ALI）中的作用及机制尚不清楚。在本研究中，我们探讨了Leo对APAP诱导的ALI的保护作用，并阐明了其分子机制。结果显示，Leo处理可减轻APAP对小鼠原代肝细胞（MPHs）的损伤，促进细胞增殖并抑制氧化应激损伤，且Leo显著改善了小鼠中APAP诱导的ALI。Leo通过降低血清天冬氨酸氨基转移酶（AST）和丙氨酸转氨酶（ALT）水平、减轻肝脏组织病理学损伤、肝细胞坏死、炎症及氧化应激诱导的损伤，在体内和体外均能保护免受APAP诱导的ALI。此外，结果表明，Leo通过降低Bax和裂解型caspase-3的表达并增加Bcl-2表达，缓解了APAP诱导的肝细胞坏死。Leo通过激活核因子E2相关因子2（Nrf2）通路，促进Nrf2核转位并上调肝组织中氧化应激相关蛋白表达，从而减轻了APAP诱导的氧化应激损伤。此外，结果提示，Leo通过抑制Toll样受体4（TLR4）和NLR家族含吡啉结构域3（NLRP3）通路，抑制了APAP诱导的肝脏炎症。另外，Leo促进了ALI小鼠肝组织中磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（PI3K）/AKT信号通路的激活。网络药理学、分子对接和蛋白质印迹分析显示，PI3K是Leo治疗ALI的潜在靶点。分子对接和细胞热位移分析（CETSA）表明，Leo能稳定结合PI3K蛋白。总之，Leo通过调节PI3K/AKT信号通路，减轻了ALI，并逆转了肝细胞坏死、炎症反应和氧化应激诱导的损伤。
